answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut and 14-day renewal window create acute pressure, but the 94% line utilization eliminates switching or second-sourcing risk tolerance. Verification of memory_c2 confirms the low-cost vendor's SLA unreliability—they cannot be primary for critical lines. Verification of memory_c6 confirms that multi-year commitments with the incumbent unlock volume pricing that may satisfy cost pressure without disruption. Memory_c4 shows renegotiation recovered real margin at renewal. Combining these: aggressive renegotiation with the incumbent leveraging multi-year commitment (c6) and benchmarking discipline (c4) is the highest-probability path to meet the 18% target while preserving the stable integration (c1) that keeps the line at 94% utilization. This avoids the SLA hazard of c2 and preserves optionality for the next cycle. Risk: negotiation may fail to close the full 18% gap within 14 days, requiring short-term deferral or partial acceptance.
